title: External Monitoring
markdown:
`openexecutive.monitoring` watches the outside world on a heartbeat and turns detected changes into briefing proposals via the same alert pipeline that handles inbound email and Slack.

The `external_monitor_scan` heartbeat (`__internal__` channel, default every 5 min) walks `list_watchlist(enabled_only=True)`, skipping rows fresher than their per-source cadence floor. For each due row it fires a read-only source adapter resolved from `_REGISTRY` by `signal_type`:

- `vendor_status` — Statuspage Atom incident feeds (AWS, Stripe, GitHub, …).
- `rss` — generic Atom/RSS via feedparser (changelogs, layoffs.fyi, filings).
- `stock` — Yahoo Finance chart endpoint; fires on `abs_change_pct_gte` moves.
- `page_watch` — change-detection on a feed-less page. Fetches via the keyless httpx fetcher by default, or via xcrawl's scrape API when the row carries `config.fetch = "xcrawl"` — so JS-rendered / bot-blocked pages that publish no RSS (most modern news / marketing sites) are still monitorable.
- `edgar` and the BILLED `query` web-search adapter.

Each `Signal` is trigger-filtered, severity-clamped to the row's `[floor, ceiling]`, and INSERTed into `external_signals` where `UNIQUE(dedup_key)` drops replays. Survivors pass a suppression cascade (`dry_run` → `below_floor` → capture-time relevance enrichment → promote), then `promote_signal_to_alert` builds an `AlertEvent` handed to `alerts.pipeline.schedule_evaluation` and surfaced as a `/today` proposal.

The `query` adapter is a special case: it emits every web hit flat-LOW (it can't judge materiality per-hit), so for query signals enrichment runs BEFORE the floor gate and `_grade_query_severity` regrades from the relevance read (≥0.8 HIGH, ≥0.5 MEDIUM, else LOW). Without this, any query watch item with a `severity_floor` above LOW would suppress every hit — which is what left the Monitoring section empty even while standing queries were returning material findings.

Which lane a proposal lands in is decided by `briefing.ranking.categorize`: an unrouted, low/medium signal from a monitoring source (`stock`, `vendor_status`, `rss`, `query`, `edgar`, `page_watch`, or any `external:*` topic tag) is `monitoring` (the collapsible Monitoring section); a routed or high/urgent one is `action` (the "Needs you" queue). The triage prompt's External Signals rule covers all six source kinds so it trusts the source and emits the `external:*` tags that drive this split.

The watchlist is editable from chat (`add_watchlist_entry`, `tune_watchlist_entry`) and HTTP (`/watchlist`); the `executive_research` workflow proposes what to watch. Because that workflow is LLM-driven and historically proposed feed URLs it never verified (most were dead — 404 / 403 / not-actually-a-feed), every `rss` target is validated at insert time (`monitoring.target_validation`): a URL that fetches and parses as a feed is kept; a public page that isn't a feed is converted to a scrape-backed `page_watch` when xcrawl can read it, otherwise rejected (HTTP 422 / tool error); SSRF-blocked or unparseable URLs are rejected outright and never handed to xcrawl. Non-`rss` types insert unchanged with no network I/O.

### Invariants

- Adapters are read-only — they never write upstream and never auto-execute.
- Every `Signal` carries a deterministic `dedup_key` and a mandatory `provenance_url`.
- Fetches are SSRF-guarded and bounded by `external_monitor_max_fetch_bytes`; xcrawl scrape (off by default, gated by `XCRAWL_ENABLED` + `XCRAWL_API_KEY`) is the one path that delegates the fetch to an external API.
- Suppressed signals are still persisted so audits show the full picture.
